segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Well, Don, we are gonna talk for a while.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏞᎦᏛ ᏙᏓᏓᏝᏃᎮᏟ and uh...ᏓᎬᏯᏛ.ᏛᎮᏢᏂ ᎠᎬᏳᏃ ᎨᏒ ‘Ꮩ ᏕᏣᏙᎠ, ᏳᏁᎦ ᎬᏗ?
segments.transliteration: tlegadv dodadatlanohetli and uh...dagvyadv.dvhetlvni agvyuno gesv ‘do detsadoa, yunega gvdi?
segments.translation: We are going to talk for a while. And uh… I’m going to ask you questions. First of all, what is your English name?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Your English name, what is it?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: My English name is Toney.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Toney. Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Cornshucker.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Cornshucker. Yeah, mhm. ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎾ ᏕᏣᏙᎠ ‘Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ?
segments.transliteration: Cornshucker. Yeah, mhm. atsalagina detsadoa ‘do usdi?
segments.translation: Cornshucker. Yeah, mm-hmm. What is your Cherokee name?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Dona.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᎾ, ᏙᎾ, yeah. ᎭᏢ ᏣᏕᏁ ᎨᏎ?
segments.transliteration: dona, dona, yeah. hatlv tsadene gese?
segments.translation: Dona, yeah. Where were you born?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Over there across the creek.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Across the creek, yeah. Is that where you were born --

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Across the creek? Yeah. What year were you born?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: What is it?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What year were you born?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏅᎩᏍᎪᎯ, mhm, yeah...mhm. ᎥᏄᎨ. ᎡᏍᎦᏂ, ᏣᏛ.ᏏᏙᎸ?
segments.transliteration: nvgisgohi, mhm, yeah...mhm. vnuge. esgani, tsadv.sidolv?
segments.translation: ’40, yeah. Were you raised around here?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, uh huh.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: I went to one school.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, right there?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: How long did you go to school?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Four years, then I went to Colcord.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Colcord, yeah.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: When I was in tenth grade a truck fell on me.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Really? Well, I’ll be…

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: So I didn’t finish school.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What happened when the truck fell on you?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: Uh...ᏭᎵᏬᏍᏔᏁᎴᏛ Ꮎ ᏃᏭ ᏂᎦᏓ ‘out of control...wouldn’t start, and no brakes.’
segments.transliteration: Uh...wuliwostaneledv na nowu nigada ‘out of control...wouldn’t start, and no brakes.’
segments.translation: It died on me. It went out of control. It wouldn’t start and no brakes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Huh.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: We came down a high hill and we couldn’t make the curve and the truck flipped over.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, man.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᏦᎢ ᏃᏥᎥ ᎣᎦᏣᎥ ᎠᎯᎵᏙᎯ Ꮭ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏱᏄᎵᏍᏓᏁᎴ
segments.transliteration: tsoi notsiv ogatsav ahilidohi tla gusdi yinulisdanele
segments.translation: There were three of us. And nothing happened to the driver.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: [laughs] It was just you that got hurt?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: Huh uh. ᏔᎵᏁ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᏅᏟ Ꭲ ‘hospital’Ꭲ ᎣᎩᎾᏕᏴᎸ ᏅᎩ ᏧᏒᎯᏢ ᎠᏎᏃ ‘ᏢᏛ ‘twelve...fourteen months’ ᏱᎩ Ꭹ.Ꮃ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎨᏙ ᏥᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ...ᏥᏐᎯ ᏚᎵ,ᏍᏆᎵ,Ꮢ ᎣᏂ ᏗᏢ
segments.transliteration: Huh uh. taline tsosdadanvtli i ‘hospital’i oginadeyvlv nvgi tsusvhitlv aseno ‘tlvdv ‘twelve...fourteen months’ yigi gi.la osda gedo tsinuli,stanv...tsisohi duli,squali,sv oni ditlv
segments.translation: Huh uh. My brother and I went to the hospital and stayed four days. But about twelve or fourteen months we were crippled up. My back broke.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Man! [whistles]

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: It’s crooked now.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, man.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Backbone.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Man. ᎠᎭᏂᏭ ᎡᏙᎲ ᏗᎨᏣᎦᏴᎵᎨ. ᏗᎨᏣᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎭᏂᏭ ᎡᏙᎲ Ꭱ-Ꮧ-Ꭱ ᏣᏛ.ᏏᏙᎸ ᏥᎦᏗ Ꮭ ᎮᎾ ᎤᏨᏘᏅ’Ꮲ ᏂᏗᏣᏓᎴᏅᎮ ᎠᎭᏂᏭ ᎯᎠ?
segments.transliteration: Man. ahaniwu edohv digetsagayvlige. digetsagayvlige tsigehv ahaniwu edohv e-di-e tsadv.sidolv tsigadi tla hena utsvtinv’tlv niditsadalenvhe ahaniwu hia?
segments.translation: Man. Your parents they were just around here, so you just grew up around here and nowhere else?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Huh uh.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ‘Ꮲ ᎮᏅ ᏗᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᏗ ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ Ꭹ.Ꮃ Arkansas ᏗᏢ ᏓᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎸ
segments.transliteration: ‘tlv henv digilvwisdanedi nuli,stanv gi.la Arkansas ditlv dagilvwisdanelv
segments.translation: When I was able to work, I moved to Arkansas, and I was working around there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Arkansas...yeah. ‘Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎭᏛᏁᎮ ᎨᎮ Arkansas ᏗᏢ
segments.transliteration: Arkansas...yeah. ‘do usdi hadvnehe gehe Arkansas ditlv
segments.translation: Arkansas, yeah. What did you do around Arkansas?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Uh…chicken plantᎢ.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, chicken plant, yeah, yeah…

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: And a hatchery, where they had chickens.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh yeah, uh huh.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: Me and Charlie worked for twenty years.
segments.transliteration: Me and Charlie worked for twenty years.
segments.translation: Me and Charlie worked for twenty years.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ’twenty years yeah, mhm’ ᏍᎩᎾ ‘Ꮩ ᎬᎾ ᏄᏛᎿᏕᎨ ᏣᎵ?
segments.transliteration: ’twenty years yeah, mhm’ sgina ‘do gvna nudvhnadege tsali?
segments.translation: Twenty years, yeah, mhm. How is Charlie now?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: How is Charlie now? Is he doing alright?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Mm-hmm. They sit him up in a bed all day.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: He watches television all the time.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah. How many children did you have?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Three.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏦᎢ. Mhm. Yeah. ᏃᏊᎴᎾ ᎯᎳ ᎾᏂᎡ ᎢᏣᏝᏅᏢ?
segments.transliteration: tsoi. Mhm. Yeah. noquulena hila nanie itsatlanvtlv?
segments.translation: Three. Mm-hmm. How many siblings do you have?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: There were four of us.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What was your mother’s name?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What was your parents’ names? Your mother?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: My mom? Lali.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎳᎵ, ᏚᏙᎡ, yeah. ᎯᎳ ᏄᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᎨᎮ ᏧᏂᎩᏒ ᏍᎩᎾ?
segments.transliteration: lali, dudoe, yeah. hila nudetiyvda gehe tsunigisv sgina?
segments.translation: Lali was her name. Yeah. How old was she when she passed?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᏙᏍᏊ Ꮭ ᏱᎦᎦᏗ 85 ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᎠᎯᎵ ᏣᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᎨᎲ ᏝᏍᏊ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ.
segments.transliteration: dosquu tla yigagadi 85 yudetiyvda ahili tsagayvlige gehv tlasquu yawanata.
segments.translation: I think probably 85. That’s what I think, I don’t really know.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: 85, yeah. ᎾᏃᎲ ᏐᎢ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏤᎲ Birdchopper ᏧᏙᎢᏓ
segments.transliteration: 85, yeah. nanohv soi agayvlige tsehv Birdchopper tsudoida
segments.translation: 85, yeah. Now the other lady, she was called Birdchopper.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: My grandma?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᏣᎵᏏᏛ ᎨᎲ ᏙᎲ, yeah. ᎯᎳ ᏍᏊ ᎯᎳ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᎨᎲ ᎤᏂᎩᏒ?
segments.transliteration: Yeah, tsalisidv gehv dohv, yeah. hila squu hila yudetiyvda gehv unigisv?
segments.translation: So that was your grandma? How old was she when she passed?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Some people say she was 114 years old.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᏃᏊᎴ Ꮎ ᎯᏲᎵᎦᏛ Ꮎ ‘Rock’ ᏓᏃᎮᎰ ᏗᎧᏃᎩᏍᎩ
segments.transliteration: noquule na hiyoligadv na ‘Rock’ danoheho dikanogisgi
segments.translation: And also, you know the singer they call Rock?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: M-hmm, mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎠᎩᎶᎯᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎥᎾᎾ ‘Grandma’Ꭲ Ꭰ’ᏗᏢ ‘horseback’ ᏥᏧᏣᏭ ᏥᎨᎮ ᏣᏓ ᎦᏳᎳ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᎨᎲ ᏣᏗᏍᎬ “She had to be 130 years old,” ᏣᏓ
segments.transliteration: agilohisdi gehv vnana ‘Grandma’i a’ditlv ‘horseback’ tsitsutsawu tsigehe tsada gayula agayvlige gehv tsadisgv “She had to be 130 years old,” tsada
segments.translation: He used to stop by there, Grandma’s place, on horseback. I was just a young boy. And he said, “She was already old. She had to be 130 years old,” he said.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Man!

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᎠᎩ.ᏃᏎᎸ ᎨᎲ ᎠᎩᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎩᎵᏏᏭ ᎠᏩᏛ.ᎯᏍᏔᏅ Ꮎ Trail of Tears Ꮷ-ᏧᎶᏒ
segments.transliteration: tsiquisdi agi.noselv gehv agilisi tsigehv agilisiwu awadv.histanv na Trail of Tears tsu-tsulosv
segments.translation: My grandma told me a lot of things, she was the one that raised me. She came through the Trail of Tears.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮷ-...ᎾᏍ ᏧᎶᏒ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎨᏯ? Well, I’ll be...
segments.transliteration: tsu-...nas tsulosv sgina ageya? Well, I’ll be...
segments.translation: She came through the Trail of Tears, that woman? Well, I’ll be...

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: Uh uh. ‘Ꮲ Tennessee ᏍᎩ ᎤᏛᏅ ᏧᎾᏂᎩᏒ ᎤᏂᏣᏘ ᏥᎨᎲ “ᏦᎢ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᏛᏲᏥᎶᏒ,” ᏣᏓ
segments.transliteration: Uh uh. ‘tlv Tennessee sgi udvnv tsunanigisv unitsati tsigehv “tsoi tsudetiyvda dvyotsilosv,” tsada
segments.translation: She stayed in Tennessee somewhere and there were a lot of them. “It took us three years to get to here,” she said.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Well, I’ll be...

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: “When somebody died, we just buried them right there,” she said.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What was it like coming through the Trail?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What was it like coming through the Trail?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: Ꮭ ᏭᏟ ᎢᎦ...Ꮭ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏯᎩ.ᏃᏎᎴ...ᏥᏧᏣᎥᏭ ᎮᎾ ᎨᎮ Ꮭ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎠᏩ,Ꮫ.ᏓᏍᏗᏍᏗ ᏁᎲ ᏥᎨᎰ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᏭ ᏤᎲ ᎠᏯ ᎾᎯᏳ ... ᏲᏎ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏯᎩ.ᏃᏎᎸ ᎠᏩ,Ꮫ.ᏓᏍᏗ ᏂᎦᏬᏂᎮ ᎨᎵᎰ ᎣᏂ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎣᏂᎢᎩ
segments.transliteration: tla wutli iga...tla gusdi yagi.nosele...tsitsutsavwu hena gehe tla gusdi awa,dv.dasdisdi nehv tsigeho yusdi sgiwu tsehv aya nahiyu ... yose nigada yagi.noselv awa,dv.dasdi nigawonihe geliho oni aseno oniigi
segments.translation: I was just a little boy when she was telling me things, and you know young kids don’t listen. That’s the way I was back then. It would’ve been good if I really listened to what she was telling me. But it’s too late now.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, yeah. ᎤᏍᏗᏭᎮ ᎨᎲᏃ ᏧᏂᎩᏒ... Ꮎ ᎡᏍᎦ ᏗᏢ...
segments.transliteration: Yeah, yeah. usdiwuhe gehvno tsunigisv... na esga ditlv...
segments.translation: She was a young girl when she left.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Mm-hmm. I was 25 when we lost her.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah. ᏙᏛ, yeah. ‘Ꮩ ᎮᎾ ᎡᎳᏗ ᎡᏙᎮ ᏭᏟ ᎢᎦ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.transliteration: Yeah. dodv, yeah. ‘do hena eladi edohe wutli iga sgina
segments.translation: Oh, ain’t it? Really, she was always on foot ain’t it?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎡᎳᏗ ᎡᏙᎯ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏭᏟ ᎢᎦ, yeah.
segments.transliteration: eladi edohi tsigehv wutli iga, yeah.
segments.translation: She was always on foot?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎡᎳᏗᏛ ᏗᏂᎩᏍᎪ ᏕᎦᎳᏫᏦᎯᎰ ᎠᏭ ᎠᏎᏃ--ᎠᏎᏃ ᎾᏓᏁᎸᎾ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎥᎾ ᎠᎩᎵᏏ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: eladidv dinigisgo degalawitsohiho awu aseno--aseno nadanelvna tsigehv vna agilisi tsunilawisdi gehv
segments.translation: She walked to church. Before they had the church building, they had church services at my grandma’s.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh! Yeah.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎤᏂᏣᏘ ᏴᏫ ᎾᎾᎵᏍᏗᎰ ᏓᏂᎳᏫᏥᏙᎰ ᎯᎠᏃ ᏕᎦᏓᏁᎳ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᏦᎢᎭ ᏱᏗᏯ
segments.transliteration: unitsati yvwi nanalisdiho danilawitsidoho hiano degadanela tsunilawisdi tsoiha yidiya
segments.translation: There were people that came for the services. And today, we have a lot of churches and three people would be in there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: I know it, I know, I know. ᎭᏅᏓᏗᎰᎨ. ᏧᎾᏁᏍᎨᎲ ᎯᎠ?
segments.transliteration: I know it, I know, I know. hanvdadihoge. tsunanesgehv hia?
segments.translation: I know it, I know, I know. Do you remember when they built this [the church]?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: Uh huh. ‘ᏢᏛ ᏦᎦᏚ’Ꮲ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎮᏍᏗ ᎰᏩ ᏯᏩᎵᏍᏉᎵᏓᏁᎲ ᎠᏪᏓᏍᏗ
segments.transliteration: Uh huh. ‘tlvdv tsogadu’tlv yawadetiyvda gehv nahiyu hesdi howa yawalisquolidanehv awedasdi
segments.translation: Uh huh. I was probably about thirteen years old. They hardly let me go there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: [laughs] You were just standing around in the way?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: That’s what they said.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: [laughs] Yeah, yeah...

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᏳᏓᎭᏛ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᏅᏟ Ꮎ ᎠᎬᏱ ᎡᎯ ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ ᎤᎵᏍᏕᎸᎲ “ᎨᎢ ᏗᏯᏖᎾ Ꮻ.Ꮿ ᏗᏍᎩᏗᎯ,” ᏍᎩ ᎢᎦ ᏥᏥᏍᏕᎵᎲ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎠᏂᏐᎢ Ꮭ ᏳᎾᏚᎸᎮ ᎠᏪᏓᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎬᎩᎨ.ᎯᏙᎲ
segments.transliteration: yudahadv tsosdadanvtli na agvyi ehi sgi hena ulisdelvhv “gei diyatena wi.ya disgidihi,” sgi iga tsitsisdelihv aseno anisoi tla yunadulvhe awedasdi gehv gvgige.hidohv
segments.translation: Sometimes my older brothers helped build it. “Go get that board for me,” he said. That’s the only way I helped. The others didn’t want me to be there, they would chase me off.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: [laughs]

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: So I just went home.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: So you just went back across.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: When I get to the water, I swam.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, yeah, yeah... ᎤᏂᎪᏗᎨ. ᏚᏂᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎮ ᎠᎭᏂ ᎠᎾᏁᏍᎨᏍᎬ?
segments.transliteration: Yeah, yeah, yeah... unigodige. dunilvwisdanehe ahani ananesgesgv?
segments.translation: Yeah, yeah, yeah... Were there a lot of them building the church?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: Ꮭ Ꮩ’. Ꮎ Calvin ᎤᏚᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎦᎵᏍᎨᏫ ᏧᏙᎢᏓ

segments.transliteration: na kawaya tsa.di anisquanagodihv na ageya nuna tsuninidi nage. wunitlvsge?
segments.translation: How about this huckleberry you talked about? How did they preserve it? Did they put it in there with the potatoes?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: She cooked them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: She cooked them.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Yes, and put them in jars.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎪᎳᏛ ᏱᏃᏭ ᎧᏩᏯ ᎢᏥᎩᏍᎬ ᏳᏓᎭ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: goladv yinowu kawaya itsigisgv yudaha dohv?
segments.translation: I guess when it’s winter, you all had huckleberry to eat. Didn’t you?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Uh huh.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: She probably made a pie sometimes.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ‘Pie’ ᎴᏱᎦ ᎠᏃᏢᏍᎪ ... ᏏᏆ ᏚᎾᏝᎣ ᎠᎩᎵᏏ ‘Ꮲ ᏳᏓᎭ ᎣᏥᏱᎰ ᎣᎦᎵᏍᏓᏴᏗ
segments.transliteration: ‘Pie’ leyiga anotlvsgo ... siqua dunatlao agilisi ‘tlv yudaha otsiyiho ogalisdayvdi
segments.translation: Pie. Yeah, they made pies. And my grandma had a hog. Every once in a while we would kill it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: For you all to eat.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: She had neighbors and she would give them some of the meat, just helping them out.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Helping them out.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: Ꭺ.Ꭿ ᏥᎩ Ꮭ Ꭹ.Ꮆ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎬᏛᎦ
segments.transliteration: go.hi tsigi tla gi.lo sgi yigvdvga
segments.translation: Nowadays, there’s nobody that would do that.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: No.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: “Just let them be hungry,” they’ll say.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏝᏍᎪᎲ ᏳᎪᏓ Ꮿ.ᏅᏓᏗ Ꮎ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏥᏣᏛ.ᎯᏍᏗᎲ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏤᏲᏂᏙᎸ? ... ᎤᏕᎶᏆᎥ ᎡᏘᏴ ᎠᎨᏳᏣᏭ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏕᎶᏆᎥ ᎨᎲ ᎫᏍᏗ.
segments.transliteration: tlasgohv yugoda ya.nvdadi na agayvlige tsitsadv.hisdihv gusdi tseyonidolv? ... udeloquav etiyv ageyutsawu tsigehv udeloquav gehv gusdi.
segments.translation: You don’t remember some of the things that your grandma [the old lady] taught you? She learned to do things from a long time ago when she was a girl at school.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏃ Ꮭ ᏱᎬᎦᏓ ᏧᏕᎶᏆᎡ ᎠᏎᏃ Ꮎ ᏗᏣᎳᎩ ‘bible’ ᎢᎦ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎠᎦᏔᎲ ᏧᎪᎵᏰᏗ ᏃᏊᎴ ᎤᏙ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ Ᏹ.ᏯᏛ.ᎦᏁ Johnson Davis ᏧᏙᎢᏓ ᎠᎵᏣᏙᎲᏍᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏭ Ꭸ.ᏓᎵ ᏥᎦᏁᎸ ... ᏒᎯᏰᎢ ᏗᏢ ᎠᎪᏛ.Ꮧ ᎬᏩᎢᏒ ᎠᏓᏁᎸ ᏗᏢ “ᏤᎩᏃ ᏓᏯ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ ᎡᎵᏏ ... ᎾᏛ ᏩᎧ--ᏩᎧ ᎮᎾ ᎦᏥᏚ.Ꮕ ᏗᎦᏚᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏙᏥᏁᎩᎡᎰ ᎤᏅ,ᏙᏗ ‘cream’Ꭲ ᎴᏱᎦ ‘Cream’Ꭲ ᏳᎾᎵᏏᏂᏔᏅ ‘quart’Ꭲ ᏂᎩ.Ꮣ ‘butter’ ᎠᏃᏢᏍᎬ ᏍᏓᏱ ᎠᎾ--‘shake’ ᎾᏅᏁᎲ... ’butter’ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎲ ᏝᏕ--Ꮭ ᏣᎪᎲᎥ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏍᎩᎾ?
segments.transliteration: aseno tla yigvgada tsudeloquae aseno na ditsalagi ‘bible’ iga osda agatahv tsugoliyedi noquule udo tla yawanata yi.yadv.gane Johnson Davis tsudoida alitsadohvsgi tsigehv awu ge.dali tsiganelv ... svhiyei ditlv agodv.di gvwaisv adanelv ditlv “tsegino daya,” tsiyohehv elisi ... nadv waka--waka hena gatsidu.nv digaduhv sgina dotsinegieho unv,dodi ‘cream’i leyiga ‘Cream’i yunalisinitanv ‘quart’i nigi.da ‘butter’ anotlvsgv sdayi ana--‘shake’ nanvnehv... ’butter’ nigalisdihv tlade--tla tsagohvv yigehe sgina?
segments.translation: I can’t really say if that’s where she learned it. But she could read the Bible in Cherokee. And also, her brother, Johnson Davis, have you heard of him? He was a preacher. He lived right down the hill. Late in the evening, you would see him walking toward our house. “Tseg is heading this way,” I would tell my grandma. Sometimes I would put the cows up for credit in town. We would milk the cow or make cream. When they saved about a quart of cream, they would make butter. They shook it real hard when they made the butter. Have you not ever seen that?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Huh uh. No.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᏃᏊᎴ ᎤᏪᏘ ‘grease’Ꭲ Ᏻ--ᏳᏂᏁ ᎤᎨᏳᎯᏙ ᎨᎮ ᎠᎩᎵᏏ ... ᏣᎾᏔᏍ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏳᏙᏗ ᎨᎲ? ᎣᏜᏛ ᏥᎪᏢᏍᎬ ᎯᎠ ᏳᎭᎨᏗ ᎣᏝ ᏚᎰ... ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᎮᎾ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎠᏛᏁ--ᎠᏛᏁᎲ ᏥᎪᎲ ᎤᏫᏒᏅ ᏝᏍᏊ ᎦᏄᎳ ᏱᎦᎯᎪᏩᏔ ᎨᎲ ᎤᏫᏍᎦᎨᏛ ᏄᏩᏅ ᎦᏅᎦᎵᎲ Ꮎ ... ‘winter onion’Ꮧ ᏣᏂᏗᎰ ᏒᎩ Ꮎ ᎪᎳ ᏤᎲ ... ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ‘ᏢᏛ ‘6, 7 rows’ ᎠᎭᏂᏛᎮ ᏟᏗᎦᏅᎯᏗ... ᎩᎶ ᏱᎦᎷᎪ “ᎡᎵᏭ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏒᎩ ᎠᎩᎩᏍᏗ ᏱᏍᎬᏏ?” “ᏨᏌᏭ ᏩᎵᏍᏕᎳ,” ᎠᎪᎮᎰ “ᎪᎯ ᏗᎦᏂᎦ ᎥᎾᎾ,” ᎠᏗᎰ
segments.transliteration: noquule uweti ‘grease’i yu--yunine ugeyuhido gehe agilisi ... tsanatas yusdi yudodi gehv? odladv tsigotlvsgv hia yuhagedi otla duho... tsiquisdi hena gusdi advne--advnehv tsigohv uwisvnv tlasquu ganula yigahigowata gehv uwisgagedv nuwanv ganvgalihv na ... ‘winter onion’di tsanidiho svgi na gola tsehv ... sgiyusdi ‘tlvdv ‘6, 7 rows’ ahanidvhe tlidiganvhidi... gilo yigalugo “eliwu sgina svgi agigisdi yisgvsi?” “tsvsawu walisdela,” agoheho “gohi diganiga vnana,” adiho
segments.translation: And also when they had some old grease, my grandma wouldn’t waste it. Do you know what she used it for? ...She was making soap. It’d be this big, soap [unintelligible]... I have seen her do many things. And on her garden, you wouldn’t see grass in it. She made it smooth. That winter onion, that grows in the wintertime, I guess about six or seven rows about this [indicates] long. And somebody would come, “Can you give me some of that onion for me to eat?” She’d tell them, “Go get it yourself. I just left from there.”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That old lady really liked to help other people?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎤᎸᏉᏗ ᎨᏎ ᏴᏫ ᏧᏍᏕᎵᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ... ᎤᎪᏗᏛ ᏚᏍᏕᎸᎯᏙᎴ?
segments.transliteration: ulvquodi gese yvwi tsusdelidi sgina agayvlige ... ugodidv dusdelvhidole?
segments.translation: She really liked to help other people. I guess she helped a lot of people?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ... ᎩᎶᏛ ‘Ꮲ ᏛᏳᏂᎩᏓ ᎠᏴᏅᎰᎮᎰ ᏫᏙᎧᏅᏫᏍᎪ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎨᏍᏗ ᎤᏁᎫᏥᏓ ᏧᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏙᏳᏃ ᏴᏫ ᏓᏍᏕᎵᎮ
segments.transliteration: vv ... gilodv ‘tlv dvyunigida ayvnvhoheho widokanvwisgo aseno gesdi unegutsida tsulvwisdane yigehe doyuno yvwi dasdelihe
segments.translation: Uh huh. Somebody from way off would come get her and take her with them to heal someone. But she didn’t use it in a mean way, she really did help the people.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, the sick people.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎾᏭ ... Ꮎ ‘grapevines’ ᏥᏂᏚᏍᏗ ᏧᏍᏗ ᏗᎦᏐᏆᎸ ᏂᏚᏍᏙ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᏧᏩᏅᏕᎩ ᏅᏬᏘ ᎤᏬᏢᏅ ᎤᏠ ᎯᎠ ᏂᎩᏓ ‘purse’ ᎤᎳ’Ꭳ ᎥᎾ ᎤᏠ ᎢᎪᎯᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎯᏙᎰ
segments.transliteration: nawu ... na ‘grapevines’ tsinidusdi tsusdi digasoqualv nidusdo sgiyusdi tsuwanvdegi nvwoti uwotlvnv utlo hia nigida ‘purse’ ula’o vna utlo igohida tsigehv ahidoho
segments.translation: Those grapevines they have little round pieces [buds] and she would use those to make medicine and that’s what she used. She had a big purse and that’s where she kept it and had it for a long time.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What kind of medicine helped her?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᏱᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᏭᏛᎲ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏱᏚᏬᎥ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎮ ᏅᏬᏘ ᎠᏓᏙᎵᏍᏗᎰ ᎮᎾ...
segments.transliteration: yinigalisdiwudvhv yusdi yiduwov sgiyusdi nigalisdihe nvwoti adadolisdiho hena...
segments.translation: Just any kind, I guess. Just so she named it and it became medicine. She prayed over it before she used it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Man!

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ...ᏂᏚᏄᏮᎾ ... Ꮎ ᎮᎾ ‘Ꮩ ᏥᏚᏙᎥ Ꮎ Fabilo Phil ᏗᎾᏓᏅᏟ
segments.transliteration: ...nidunuwvna ... na hena ‘do tsidudov na Fabilo Phil dinadanvtli
segments.translation: What was his name? Fabilo, Phil’s brother.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Noyi.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏪᏓᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏗᎧᏂᎨᏂ ᏗᏲᎤᏟ ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: vv sgina uwedasdi gehv dikanigeni diyoutli gehv
segments.translation: That’s who would come. He had bad knees. He was crippled and they had to help him sit down.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh yeah, ᏙᏳᏛ.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: When it was time for him to go home, he’d be walking down the road.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: She really did cure him.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: There were a lot of mean people around, she said.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah... Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏅ “ᎣᏍᏗᏁᎳ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏱᎬᎿᎸᏓᏍᏗ ᎨᎮ ᎤᏍᎦᎯᏗ ᏅᏬᏘ ᎠᎦᏔᎲ,” ᏣᏗᎲ
segments.transliteration: asenv “osdinela tsigehv tla yigvhnalvdasdi gehe usgahidi nvwoti agatahv,” tsadihv
segments.translation: “My ex-husband was one of them. They couldn’t be mean to him because he made a strong medicine,” she said.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, man.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: “ᎥᎾ ᏣᏩᏕᎶᏆᎥ” ᏣᏗᎲ ‘ᎸᏢᏛ Kenwood-Ꭲ ᏗᏢ ᏓᏳᏂᎩᏓ ᏍᎩᎾ Birdchopper.
segments.transliteration: “vna tsawadeloquav” tsadihv ‘lvtlvdv Kenwood-i ditlv dayunigida sgina Birdchopper.
segments.translation: “And that’s where I learned,” she said. He came from Kenwood, Birdchopper.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, yeah! Uh huh.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎾᎮᎾ Leroy ᎠᎵᏣᏙᎲᏍᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᏪᏙᎸ ᏞᎦ ᎠᎭᏂ
segments.transliteration: nahena Leroy alitsadohvsgi tsigehv tsuwedolv tlega ahani
segments.translation: That Leroy, the preacher, that came here for a while --

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Backwater.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎥᎥ “ᎦᏥᏲᎵᎦ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏂ-‘Birdchopper’,” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎣᏍᏓ ᏅᏬᏘ ᎨᎲ,” ᏣᏗᎲ
segments.transliteration: vv “gatsiyoliga gehv sgina ani-‘Birdchopper’,” tsadihv “osda nvwoti gehv,” tsadihv
segments.translation: -- “I knew them real well, those Birdchoppers,” he said. “The medicine was good,” he said.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎮᎾ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏩᏌ uh...Backwater ᏣᎦᏔᎲ ᏅᏬᏘ.
segments.transliteration: sgihena squu uwasa uh...Backwater tsagatahv nvwoti.
segments.translation: He’s the only one, that Backwater, knew how to make medicine.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Uh huh.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎠᏓᏠᏍᎩ ᏣᏃᏎᎲ ᏥᎨᎰ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᏱᏚᏗᏂᏴ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏣᎦᏔᎲ ᏅᏬᏘ ᏍᏗᏭᏅ ᏣᏟᏍᏓ ᏯᏓᏁᎲᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮓ-ᏃᏭ ᏱᏫᎦᏅᎵᏰ ᎤᎩᏨᏓᏭᏛ ᏃᏭ ᏣᏍᎪᎸᎬ Ꮩ’ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏣᎦᏔᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏅᏬᏘ ᏣᎵᏏᏃ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏪᏲᏁ ᎨᎮ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: na adatlosgi tsanosehv tsigeho iyusdi sgiyusdi yidudiniyv osda tsagatahv nvwoti sdiwunv tsatlisda yadanehvsi tsigehv no-nowu yiwiganvliye ugitsvdawudv nowu tsasgolvgv do’ osda tsagatahv sgina nvwoti tsalisino tsigehv uweyone gehe dohv?
segments.translation: What they called, the belt, when he used it he could understand the medicine real well. He would give you just a little bitty bottle of it. And when you use it, by next morning, things were better. He really knew medicine. I guess your grandma taught him, right?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Mhm. ᎢᎳᎦᏯᏅᏙ ᎤᎪᏗ ᎠᎦᏔᎮ ᏣᎵᏏ ᏅᏬᏘ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: Mhm. ilagayanvdo ugodi agatahe tsalisi nvwoti dohv?
segments.translation: I guess your grandma really knew how to make the medicine.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: She knew a lot about how to make medicine.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: Uh huh. ᎩᎶ ‘ᎸᏢ ᏓᏳᏂᎩᏓ ‘Ꮲ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏳᏪᏍᏓᏁ ᏳᎵᏍᏓᏁ ᎴᏱᎩ ᏍᏊ ᏒᎯᏰ ᏳᎷᏨ *mumbled a name* ᎯᏲᎵᎦ ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: Uh huh. gilo ‘lvtlv dayunigida ‘tlv gusdi yusdi yuwesdane yulisdane leyigi squu svhiye yulutsv *mumbled a name* hiyoliga gehv
segments.translation: Uh huh. Somebody that come from somewhere else, when something was wrong with him, he would come, even if he came at night. [mumbled a name] did you know him?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: “ᎥᎾᎾ ᏪᏓ,” Ꮎ ᏐᏈᎵ ᏧᏂᎾᏌᏁᏍᏗ ‘wagon’ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏧᎳᏍᏛᏁ ᏣᎾᏖ ᎦᎵᏉᎩ ᏄᎾᏍᏕᏟ ᏫᏘᎦ ᎠᎪᎮᎲ
segments.transliteration: “vnana weda,” na soquili tsuninasanesdi ‘wagon’ sgina tsulasdvne tsanate galiquogi nunasdetli witiga agohehv
segments.translation: “Go get them,” he told him. “seven roots that have been run over, that you know of, by a wagon.”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Gah!

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: And today you can see him somewhere. “That was a good medicine,” he says.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Man! The one that the wagon stepped on?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᏙᏆᎴᎳ ᏚᎳᏍᏛᏅ ᏚᎾᏍᏕᏢ Ꮎ ᏙᏆᎴᎳ ᏧᎶᎯᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏫᎬᎭᎸᎥᎪᎮᎲ
segments.transliteration: vv doqualela dulasdvnv dunasdetlv na doqualela tsulohisdi sgina wigvhalvvgohehv
segments.translation: Yeah, the wagon stepped on the roots, where the wagon trail goes through. “Go cut that,”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It was medicine? Well, I’ll be...

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Some doctors really were good with the medicine.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: I think it would have been good if I had learned some of it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎦᎪ ᎤᏪᏲᏁ ᎨᏎ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏅᏬᏘ?
segments.transliteration: sgina agayvlige tsigehv gago uweyone gese sgina nvwoti?
segments.translation: And the old lady, who taught her about the medicine?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: The medicine. Her husband.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎤᎾᏁᎳᏛᎮ? Boy...ᏙᎮ ... uh... Birdchopper ᏗᏚᏙᎥ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏃᏊᎴ ᎠᏂᏁᎳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎭᏢ ᏓᏳᏓᎴᏅᏓ ᎨᎮ Birdchopper ᏚᎾᏙᎥ
segments.transliteration: unaneladvhe? Boy...dohe ... uh... Birdchopper didudov agayvlige noquule aninela tsigehv hatlv dayudalenvda gehe Birdchopper dunadov
segments.translation: Her husband. Birdchopper was her name, and her husband’s. Where did it originate, the name Birdchopper?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Where they came from.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎥᎾ ᏗᏢ mhm. ᏣᎳᎩ ᎤᏪᏘ yeah...’ᏙᎲ ‘ᏙᎲ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎦᏓᎧ ᏍᎩᎾ Birdchopper?
segments.transliteration: vna ditlv mhm. tsalagi uweti yeah...’dohv ‘dohv usdi gadaka sgina Birdchopper?
segments.translation: North Carolina, maybe. What does that mean, Birdchopper?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ‘Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎦᏓᎨ Birdchopper? ᎭᏢ--ᎭᏢ ᎤᏂᎩᏛ ᏥᎦᏗᏍᎬ ᎭᏢ ᎤᏂᎩᏛ ᎨᎮ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏚᎾᏙᎥ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎾᎮᎾ ᏓᏳᏂᎩᏓ ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: ‘do usdi gadage Birdchopper? hatlv--hatlv unigidv tsigadisgv hatlv unigidv gehe sgina dunadov tsadihv nahena dayunigida gehv
segments.translation: What does that mean, Birdchopper? What I say, where did they get the name Birdchopper?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Wherever they came from. I guess that’s the name they gave them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s where they brought it from. It sure is interesting, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Uh huh.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah. Boy...

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: Ꭴ-ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎩ,ᏗᏕ ᏧᏂᎶᏒ ᏓᎾᎵᏍᏕᎵᎰ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ...
segments.transliteration: u-usquanigi,dide tsunilosv danalisdeliho nahiyu tsigehv gohi tsigi...
segments.translation: Yeah, it was interesting the way they came. Back then, they helped each other. But today...

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: No... Mm-hmm, mm.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᏃᏊᎴ ᏯᏛᏁᏗ ᎦᏚᎩ ᏱᎩ ᎦᏂᏒᏍᏓ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏩᎾᏛᏁᎰ ᎩᎶ ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏱᎬᏴᏛ.ᎬᎦ
segments.transliteration: noquule yadvnedi gadugi yigi ganisvsda gusdi wanadvneho gilo gohi tsigi tla sgi yusdi yigvyvdv.gvga
segments.translation: It has to be a community—they plan to go help somebody and do something. But today you don’t hear about that.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Boy...ᎠᏯᏛ ᎨᏒ ᏯᏩᏚᎵ ᎤᎪᏛ ᎠᏩᏛᏓᏍᏙᏗ Ꮎ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏣᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏃᎮᏢᏅ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎩ,Ꮧ ᎤᎪᎲ ᎨᏎ ᏙᎲ? Ꮭ ‘ᎸᎯᏳ ᏣᏃᏎᎴ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎩ,Ꮧ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎤᎪᎲ Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ?
segments.transliteration: Boy...ayadv gesv yawaduli ugodv awadvdasdodi na agayvlige tsalisi tsigehv unohetlvnv noquule squu usquanigi,di ugohv gese dohv? tla ‘lvhiyu tsanosele yigehe usquanigi,di gusdi ugohv tla ilvhiyu?
segments.translation: Boy... I would really like to listen to the old lady, your grandma. What all she told and saw. She saw a lot of interesting things. Did she not ever tell you about any interesting things she saw?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᏃᏊᎴ ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ ᎩᎶ ᎣᏍᏓ--ᎣᏍᏓ ᏄᏚᏄᏩᎾ “ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏁᎵᏗ ᏚᏄᏩ,” ᏯᏓ ᏙᎲ? ᎢᎦᏓ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏱᎾᏓᏪᏏ
segments.transliteration: noquule gohi tsigi gilo osda--osda nudunuwana “sgina unelidi dunuwa,” yada dohv? igada sgina yinadawesi
segments.translation: Nowadays, when somebody is not all dressed up, they will say they got “ugly clothes on.” Ain’t it? That’s what they will say.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎠᎩᎵᏏ ᏠᎨᏏ ᏱᏓᏳᏂᎩᏓ ᏳᎵᏍᏓᏴᏅ ᎢᎦ ᎧᏫ ᏯᏗᏔ ᏙᎦᏰᏫᏒᏍᎪ ᎠᏂ-ᎠᏂᏍᎦᏯ ᏧᎾ-ᏧᎾᏑᎶ ᏧᎾᎿᏬ ᎴᏱᎦ ᏱᎦᏰᏫᏍᎪ ᏍᎩᏭ ᏄᏍᏛ
segments.transliteration: agilisi tlogesi yidayunigida yulisdayvnv iga kawi yadita dogayewisvsgo ani-anisgaya tsuna-tsunasulo tsunahnawo leyiga yigayewisgo sgiwu nusdv
segments.translation: My grandma, when she come in from the field, when she ate lunch and drank coffee. She gets the men’s clothes and sews. That’s how it was.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: “ᏓᏤᏢᏗ ᏗᏣ--ᏗᏣᎿᏬ ᏕᏣᎾ ᏍᏗ ᏕᏣᎵᏏᏂᏕᏍᏗ,” ᏕᎪᎮᎰ ᏃᏭ ᏗᎬᏍᎳᏴᏛ ᏚᎾᏄᏮ
segments.transliteration: “datsetlvdi ditsa--ditsahnawo detsana sdi detsalisinidesdi,” degoheho nowu digvslayvdv dunanuwv
segments.translation: She would tell them, “The better clothes you have, try to take care of them.” Now they were wearing clothes that were all patched up.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: [laughs]

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: Railroad ties ᎴᏱᎦ ᎠᏃᏢᏍᎪ post-Ꭲ ᎴᏱᎦ post-Ꭲ ᎦᎵᏉᎩ ᎢᏯᏓᏅᏖᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏌᏭ post ᎾᎯᏳ
segments.transliteration: Railroad ties leyiga anotlvsgo post-i leyiga post-i galiquogi iyadanvtedi tsigehv sawu post nahiyu
segments.translation: They made railroad ties, or posts. One post costed seven cents back then.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: Ꮎ railroad ties ᏥᏓᏃᏢᏍᎪ ᎦᎷᏱᏍᏗ ᎤᏍᎦᎮᏗᏛ ᎡᎮ ᎠᎩᎵᏏ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᏧᏬᏢᏗ
segments.transliteration: na railroad ties tsidanotlvsgo galuyisdi usgahedidv ehe agilisi sgiyusdi tsuwotlvdi
segments.translation: They made railroad ties with an axe, and my grandma was good at making those too.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Well, I’ll be...

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᏌᏚ--ᏌᏚ’Ꮫ ᏍᎪᎯ ᏌᏚ ᎴᏱᎦ ᏱᎾᎩᏗ (Gentry/Century) ᏱᏕᏥᏴᏫᏗ wagon ᏕᏥᎵᏗᏍᏗᎮ ᏣᏓ ᏒᎾᎴᎢ ᏯᏩᏂᎩᏒ ᏲᎩᎾᏂᎩᏒ ᎴᏱᎦ ᎩᎶ ᏃᏊᎴᏃ ᎤᏒᏍᎪ ᎣᏍᏗᎷᎪ ᏣᎾᏔ
segments.transliteration: sadu--sadu’dv sgohi sadu leyiga yinagidi (Gentry/Century) yidetsiyvwidi wagon detsilidisdihe tsada svnalei yawanigisv yoginanigisv leyiga gilo noquuleno usvsgo osdilugo tsanata
segments.translation: When I had ten or eleven made I took them to Gentry in a wagon. We left early in the morning and came home late in the evening, whoever was with me. Round-trip.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Round-trip.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎥᎾ ᎾᏕᏲᎲ ... Ꭳ ᏙᏳᏃ ᏧᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁ ᎨᎮ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏙᎲ
segments.transliteration: vna nadeyohv ... o doyuno tsulvwisdane gehe agayvlige dohv
segments.translation: Round-trip. The old lady was really a hard worker, wasn’t she?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᏍᏓᏲᏒ ᏧᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁ ᏥᎨᎲ ... ᎪᎳ ᏱᎩ Ꮎ ᎣᏏ ᏥᎸᏍᎪ ᏣᎾᏔ Ꮎ ᎠᏥᎳ “ᎯᎢ ᏱᎩᏓ ᎠᎩᎭ ᏒᏙᎾ ᏥᎧᎵᎰ,” ᏣᏓ “ᎠᏭ ᏙᎢᏃᏢᎾᎥ ᎣᎩᏂᎧᎰ,” ᏯᏓ ᎭᎴ ᏄᎦᎾᏩᏃ ᏃᏍᏓᏕᏲᎰ ᏣᏗᎲ... ᎥᎾᎮᎾ ᎠᎨ ᏌᏭ ᏥᎦᏁᎸ ᏐᎢ ᎤᏙ ᎠᎩᎵᏏ ᎥᎾ ᏞᎪ ᏣᎴᏫᏍᏗᎰ ᏣᎾᏔ ᎦᏚ ᎣᎩᏂᏁᎰ ᎣᎩᎩᏍᏗ ᏣᎾᏔ ᏗᎪᏢᏂᏍᎪ ᏣᏓ
segments.transliteration: sdayosv tsulvwisdane tsigehv ... gola yigi na osi tsilvsgo tsanata na atsila “hii yigida agiha svdona tsikaliho,” tsada “awu doinotlvnav oginikaho,” yada hale nuganawano nosdadeyoho tsadihv... vnahena age sawu tsiganelv soi udo agilisi vna tlego tsalewisdiho tsanata gadu oginineho ogigisdi tsanata digotlvnisgo tsada
segments.translation: Yeah, she worked really hard. In wintertime, she said she had a bucket and she took the ashes out of the stove, they set it in the middle of the room and kept warm. And there was another one living close by, her brother. My grandma. Her brother would stop by every now and then and he would give us bread someone had baked for us to eat.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, well, I’ll be...

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎥᎾᏴ ᎠᎾᏂᎩᏍᎬ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏙᏆᎴᎷ ᎠᏂᎳᏫᏥᏙᎮ ... ᎩᏟ ᏙᏥᎾᏝᎥ ᏣᎾᏔ ‘ᎸᏢ ᏛᏳᏂᎶᏒ ᎬᏩᏝᏫᏍᏓᏂᏢ ᎩᏟ ᏣᎾᏔ “ᏙᏥᏅᏮᏅ,” ᏣᏗᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎩᏟ ᏯᏛᏁᏗ Ꮎ “ᏥᎩᎵ ᏗᏓᏟᎶᏍᏗᏍᎩ ᏱᎩ ᎩᎶ ᏴᏫ ᎩᎳᏴᏛ ᏯᎾᏕᎳᎰ,” ᏣᏓ
segments.transliteration: vnayv ananigisgv ahani doqualelu anilawitsidohe ... gitli dotsinatlav tsanata ‘lvtlv dvyunilosv gvwatlawisdanitlv gitli tsanata “dotsinvwvnv,” tsadihv sgina gitli yadvnedi na “tsigili didatlilosdisgi yigi gilo yvwi gilayvdv yanadelaho,” tsada
segments.translation: They were leaving from here in a wagon going to church. I had dogs, they just came and stayed with me. She said she “Fixed them up to where if a ts(i)gili would come around, the dogs would know.”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Gah!

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᏃᏭ ᏌᏭ...ᏦᎩᎳᏫᏥᏙᏅ “ᏃᏭᏛ ᎢᎦᏂᎩᏍᏗ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎥᎩᏙ ᏣᎾᏔ ᏃᏭ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎤᎵᏎᎩ ᏥᏂᎦᎵᏗᎲ ᏧᎵᏒᏍᎪ ᏚᏪᏲᏎᎸ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎩᏟ Ꭱ’ᎯᏛ ᏲᎦᏂᎩᏒ ᎠᎬᏱ ᎠᎢᏐ ᏌᏭ ᏣᎾᏔ ᏐᎢ ᎣᏂ ᏃᏭ ᎠᎾᏓᏁᏟᏴᏍᎪ ᏣᎾᏔ
segments.transliteration: nowu sawu...tsogilawitsidonv “nowudv iganigisdi,” tsiyohelv vgido tsanata nowu nahiyu ulisegi tsinigalidihv tsulisvsgo duweyoselv sgina gitli e’hidv yoganigisv agvyi aiso sawu tsanata soi oni nowu anadanetliyvsgo tsanata
segments.translation: So one time after we’d been to church. “I guess we better go home,” I said to my sister. Just when it was getting dark out. The dogs were getting restless as we left. One was walking in front, the other in the back of the wagon. Then they would trade places.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Huh!

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎠᏭᏴ Ꭸ.ᏓᎵᏃ ᎣᎩᎷᏨ ᎩᎳ--ᎩᎳᏴ ᎤᏝᎢᏍᏔᏅ ᎣᏂ ᎡᏙᎲ ᏣᎾᏔ ᏚᏂᏘᎷᏅ ᎩᏟ ᏣᎾᏔ ᎤᎾᏕᎳᎰᏒ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎡᏙᎲ
segments.transliteration: awuyv ge.dalino ogilutsv gila--gilayv utlaistanv oni edohv tsanata dunitilunv gitli tsanata unadelahosv gusdi edohv
segments.translation: When we got down the hill, this one dog ran by fast. They both looked up cause they knew something was there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: ...was there.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏅ ᎠᏯᏄᎵ ᎨᎮ ᎠᎩᎵᏏ ᏳᏓᎾᏫᏍᏔᎾ ... “ᎥᏍᏊ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏛᏂ--ᏛᏂᏂᏴᎯ ᎠᏬ--ᎠᏩᏛᏅ,” ᏣᏓ ... ᎠᎹᏯ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎯᎪᎥᏍ ᎨᎮ?
segments.transliteration: asenv ayanuli gehe agilisi yudanawistana ... “vsquu gusdi dvni--dvniniyvhi awo--awadvnv,” tsada ... amaya tsigehv higovs gehe?
segments.translation: I guess my grandma was fast when she ran. “They are going to catch something,” I said. Did you ever see Amaya before?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: She had one arm.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎾᏅ ᎠᎩᏥ “ᏛᎯᎯᎵᎴᏒᎢ” ᎦᎵᏦᏕᏛ ᏩᏩᎵᏒᏍᏔᏅ ᏣᎾᏔ ᎠᏭ-ᎠᏭᏴ ᎠᎹᏱ ᏗᎦᏐᏨ ᏗᏢ ᏅᏲ ᏥᎩ ᎥᎾᎾ ᎤᏁᎫᎩᏍᏗ ᎠᎹ ᎤᏗᏔᏗᏍᏗ ᎠᎩᎵᏏ ᎥᎾᏴ ᏫᏚᏂᎦᏐᏍᏔᏅ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎠᏥᎩᎵ Ꮎ ᏎᎷ ᏓᎩᏫᏒ ᏃᏊᎴ ᎠᏭ ᏗᏢ ᎨᎢ Ꭹ-ᎩᎶ ᏗᎦᏁᎳ ᎠᎨ ... ᏍᎩᏛ ᎠᎩᏙᏓ ᏗᎾᏓᏅᏟ ᏥᎦᏁᎳ ᏍᎩᏃᏅ ᎤᏍᎦᎮᏗ ᎨᎮ ᎠᏥᎩᎵ
segments.transliteration: nanv agitsi “dvhihililesvi” galitsodedv wawalisvstanv tsanata awu-awuyv amayi digasotsv ditlv nvyo tsigi vnana unegugisdi ama uditadisdi agilisi vnayv widunigasostanv tsadihv sgina gusdi atsigili na selu dagiwisv noquule awu ditlv gei gi-gilo diganela age ... sgidv agidoda dinadanvtli tsiganela sginonv usgahedi gehe atsigili
segments.translation: And my mom said, “You drive.” And I took off running into the house. Right by the house there was a creek with a big rock, that’s where she got her water, my grandma. Whatever it was, they chased it down there, the ts(i)gili. I had a corn field and somebody lived nearby. That was my dad’s brother that lived there. And he was a very good ts(i)gili.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Hmm.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: “Ꮎ...ᏛᏍᏊ--ᏛᏂᏟ ᎩᎳ ᎠᏂᏂᏴᎲ ᎩᏟ,” ᎠᏩ-ᎠᏩᏛᏅ ᏣᎾᏔ ᎠᏩᏁᎷᎩᏒ ᏣᏗᎲ “ᏙᏳᏅ ᏚᏮᏂᏴᎲ ᏣᏓ ᏃᏊᎴ Ꮪ-ᏚᎵᏘᎴᏎ,” ᏣᏓ ... Ꭱ...Ꭱ...ᏗᏓᏁᎵᏃ “they had ‘em tree’d,” ᏧᏛᏅ ᏩᏩᏗᏠᎸ ᏣᏗᎲ “ᏪᏌ ᎤᎩᎸ,” ᏣᏓ ᎠᎩᎪᎥᏃ ᏪᏌ ᏓᏳᏙᏒ ᏣᎾᏔ ᎤᏩᏂᏴᎲ Ꮿ ᏙᏳ ᏕᎣᏍᎦᏏᎸᎥ Ꮎ ᎩᏟ ᏣᎾᏔ ᎥᎾ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᎭᏫᏂ ᏭᏕᎵᏨ ᏣᎾᏔ...Ꮎ...ᏔᎵᎭ ᏫᏄᏒᏟ, ᎤᏛᏂᎳ ᎨᎲ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎠᏎᏛ ᎥᎩᏑᏰᏒ ᏫᏥᎦᎦᏎᏍᏙᏗ ᏣᎾᏔ ᏃᏭ...ᏃᏭ ᎪᎯᏳ ᏭᏲᎱᎯᏍᏗ ᎨᎮ ᏣᎾᏔᏃ ... ᏥᎪᏱ ᎤᎾᎴᏅᎲ ᎠᏂᏅᎪᎬ ᎠᎰᎵ ᏣᎾᏔ
segments.transliteration: “na...dvsquu--dvnitli gila aniniyvhv gitli,” awa-awadvnv tsanata awanelugisv tsadihv “doyunv duwvniyvhv tsada noquule du-dulitilese,” tsada ... e...e...didanelino “they had ‘em tree’d,” tsudvnv wawaditlolv tsadihv “wesa ugilv,” tsada agigovno wesa dayudosv tsanata uwaniyvhv ya doyu deosgasilvv na gitli tsanata vna galitsode hawini wudelitsv tsanata...na...taliha winusvtli, udvnila gehv tsadihv asedv vgisuyesv witsigagasesdodi tsanata nowu...nowu gohiyu wuyohuhisdi gehe tsanatano ... tsigoyi unalenvhv aninvgogv aholi tsanata
segments.translation: “They probably will kill it, if they catch it” I thought. She said, “They caught it for a while, but it got loose.” When I got to the house, they had ‘em tree’d. And it was a cat. As soon as the cat saw me, it jumped toward me. The dogs got hold of the cat, but it got loose and ran underneath the house. After a few days, the cat was limping around. And they picked me to take care of the cat. And after a while it was going to die, bugs started coming out of its mouth.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Gah lee.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᏃᏊᎴ ᏕᎦᏙᏍᎬ ᎤᎴᏅᎲ ᏣᎾᏔ ᎦᎾᏰᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏣᎾᏔ
segments.transliteration: noquule degadosgv ulenvhv tsanata ganayegi tsigehv tsanata
segments.translation: And then they started falling out. And it was scary.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Man! So it wasn’t around too long?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: So it wasn’t around too long?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Huh uh. The dogs were bad.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Gah lee. Man!

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎪᎯᎩ ... ᏍᏗᎩᏓ ᎢᏓᏛᏁᎵᏍᎩᏭ ᏥᎨᎲ ...Ꭰ-ᎠᏂ-ᎠᎾᏦᏎᏍᎪ ᏧᎾᏚ.ᎩᏍᏗ ᎤᎾᏚᎵᎲ ᎦᏳᎳ ᏥᏂᏕᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎰ “canning factory” “ᏗᏣᏚ.ᎩᏍᏗ ᎢᏣᏚᎵ?” ᎦᏥᏲᎲ “ᏫᏕᏥᏯᏘᏂᏓᏛ,” ᏃᏱ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎣᏏ ᎢᎦ ᎠᏕᎳ ᏳᏠ ᏳᏓᎭ “ᎠᏯᏛ ᎠᏩᏚᎵ ᎠᏩᏗᏔᏍᏗ,” ᏙᎦᏘᏂᏛ ᏩᏚᎵᏏ ᏫᎦᎷᏨᏅ “liquor store” ᎯᎢ ᏗᏢ ᎠᎩ---ᏭᏴ--ᏭᏕᎵᎬ ᏗᏢ ᏥᏫᎦᏅᏅ ᏫᎧᎿᎷᏐᏅ “junk pile” ᏥᎪᏢ...
segments.transliteration: gohigi ... sdigida idadvnelisgiwu tsigehv ...a-ani-anatsosesgo tsunadu.gisdi unadulihv gayula tsinidegilvwisdaneho “canning factory” “ditsadu.gisdi itsaduli?” gatsiyohv “widetsiyatinidadv,” noyi tsigehv osi iga adela yutlo yudaha “ayadv awaduli awaditasdi,” dogatinidv wadulisi wigalutsvnv “liquor store” hii ditlv agi---wuyv--wudeligv ditlv tsiwiganvnv wikahnalusonv “junk pile” tsigotlv...
segments.translation: Back in the day when we were young and could do anything, they were acting anxious, wanting something to drink. I was already working at the canning factory. I asked them, “Do you all want something to drink? I’ll go buy it.” Noyi (that was) he always had a little money. He said he wanted something to drink. I took him to Southwest City, Missouri, we got to the liquor store and there was a road on the west side. When you get to the top there was a junk pile.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, yeah.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Did you ever go there?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ...Ꮎ ᏚᏂᏁᎩᏒ ᏧᎾᏗᏔᏍᏗ ᏃᏱ ᏥᎨᎲ “ᏓᎬᏅᏁᎵ ᏣᏗᏔᏍᏗ,” “ᎭᏩ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎯᎢ ᏱᎩᏓ ᎠᏟᏍᏛ ᏫᏍᎩ ᎠᎩᏁᏁᎸ “’tail hood’ ᏫᏢᎲᎩ ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎠᏭ ᎮᎾ ᏯᎦᏝᏂ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏳᎾᎩᏟᏗ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ... “ᏱᏣᏛᏅᎢᏍᏔᎾ ᏱᏓᏂᎦ,” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ ... ᎩᎶ ᏳᏁᎦ ᎤᎷᏨ ᏦᏍᏓᏛ *divan loveseat*Ꭲ ‘ᏙᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ... Ꭰ-Ꭰ-ᎠᏭ ᏛᎾᏛᏅᏕᏒ “ᏗᏣᏚᎵ ᏕᎬᏗᏏ,” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ “ᎭᏩ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎣᎬᏁᎴ ᎡᎵᏭ ᎣᎩᏢᏛ Ꮎ *divan* Ꮎ *loveseat* ᎣᏂ ᏗᏢ ᏍᏓᏱ ᏛᏲᏥᏍᏙᎡ
segments.transliteration: ...na duninegisv tsunaditasdi noyi tsigehv “dagvnvneli tsaditasdi,” “hawa,” tsiyohelv hii yigida atlisdv wisgi aginenelv “’tail hood’ witlvhvgi tsiyohelv awu hena yagatlani sgina yunagitlidi,” tsiyohelv ... “yitsadvnvistana yidaniga,” gatsiyohelv ... gilo yunega ulutsv tsosdadv *divan loveseat*i ‘dogi yusdi... a-a-awu dvnadvnvdesv “ditsaduli degvdisi,” awohelv “hawa,” tsiyohelv gusdi ogvnele eliwu ogitlvdv na *divan* na *loveseat* oni ditlv sdayi dvyotsisdoe
segments.translation: They got something to drink. And Noyi said, “I’m going to give you a drink to drink.” “Okay,” I said. He was giving me a bottle of whiskey this big [gesture]. I told him to put it on the tail hood of the car. If they could see it, they’ll have it pointed out. “When you all get ready, we’ll go home,” I told them. Some white people drove up; they had a very good divan and a loveseat. They were going to throw them away, but they said, “If you want them, we’ll give them to you.” So, I took them. We did something, and put the divan in the truck and the loveseat we put in the back.

segments.text: ᎡᎵᏭᏛ ᎣᎩᏩᏛᎮ ᏲᎦᏛᏁᏗ ᎣᎦᏦᏗ ᏃᏭ ᏛᎣᏣᏂᎩᏒ ᎨᎢ Mayfield ᎡᏍᎦ ᏗᏢ Ꮎ *dirt road* ᏗᎦᏅᏅ ... Dixon’Ꮫ ᏥᏚᏙᎥ Ꮎ ᏧᎾᏓᏂᏐᏗ

segments.translation: Somehow we found a way to get in to go back home. Over there by Mayfield there’s a dirt road, the cemetery is named Dixon.

segments.translation: Have you been there?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎤᎿ ᏦᎦᏕᏯᏛ ᎨᎢ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎬᎿᎨ Ꮹ--ᎤᏓᏴᎳᏙᏒ “*What was it?*” ᎤᏛᏅ Wally ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎩᏍᏓᏩᏛᎲ “*If it’s a dog, I want it,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “*Yeah, it’s a pup,*” ᎯᎢ ᏂᎦᏘ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎩᏟ Ꮭ ᏱᎬᏱᎦ ᎤᏥ Ꮷ--ᎠᏍᏓᏩᏛᎲ ᏳᏩᎴᎾᏢ ᎥᏥᏯᏘᏃᏢᏃ ᎠᎩᎵᏏ ᏤᎲ ᎤᏬᏢ “ᎠᏯ--ᎠᏯ ᎬᏯ--ᎬᏯᏛᎯᏍᏓᏌ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎩᏟ,” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ ᎠᏕᎶᎰᏍᎬᏃ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎨᎮ ᎩᏟ
segments.transliteration: uhna tsogadeyadv gei gusdi gvhnage wa--udayvladosv “*What was it?*” udvnv Wally tsigehv agisdawadvhv “*If it’s a dog, I want it,” tsiyohelv “*Yeah, it’s a pup,*” hii nigati sgina gitli tla yigvyiga utsi tsu--asdawadvhv yuwalenatlv vtsiyatinotlvno agilisi tsehv uwotlv “aya--aya gvya--gvyadvhisdasa sgina gitli,” awohelv adelohosgvno osda gehe gitli
segments.translation: When we come around there, we saw a black shadow. “What was it?” said Wally. He was with me. “If it’s a dog, I want it,” I told him. “Yeah, it’s a pup,” he said. It was a little pup; probably he got lost following his mom. I took him home, and Grandma was there. She said, “Let me raise the dog for you.” She knew it would be a good dog. She had been watching for about a month.

segments.translation: What did you name the dog?

segments.translation: His name? Jim.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏥᎻᏍ ᏚᏙᎡ? Yeah. ᎣᏍᏓ’Ꭾ ᎧᏃᎭᎵᏙᎯ ᎤᏟᎢᎶᏞ?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᎡᏣᏙ ᏥᏙᎩᎾᏓᏩᏛᎮ ᏣᎩᏍᏓᏩᏙᏞ “ᎦᎪ ᏄᏩᏅ ᎩᏟ,” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ “ᎠᏯ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᎣᏍᏗ--ᎣᏍᏗ ᏱᎵᏃᎮᏔᎾ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏫᏍᏓᎵᎢ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ Ꮎ ᏦᎩᎾᏂᎩᏒ (Gentry/Century) ᎾᎥ ᏥᏬᏍᏗᏁᎸ ... ᏳᏓᎭ ᏅᎩ ᏦᏍᎪᎯ ᎦᏂᎩᏍᎬ ᏓᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎴᎬ ᎤᏙᏓᏩᏓ ... “ᏣᎾᏖᏍ?” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ “ᏱᏫᏕᏣᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎴ ᎠᏭ *front door* ᎠᏂᏒᏍᎪ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎩᏟ,” ᏣᏗᎲ “Ꮭ ᎩᎶ ᏱᎬᏴᎯ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᎨᎮ,” ᏣᏓ ‘ᏙᏳ ᏱᏙᏘᎷᎦ ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: na agayvlige etsado tsidoginadawadvhe tsagisdawadotle “gago nuwanv gitli,” awohelv “aya,” tsiyohelv “osdi--osdi yilinohetana sgina wisdalii,” tsiyohelv na tsoginanigisv (Gentry/Century) nav tsiwosdinelv ... yudaha nvgi tsosgohi ganigisgv dagilvwisdanelegv udodawada ... “tsanates?” awohelv “yiwidetsalvwisdanele awu *front door* anisvsgo sgina gitli,” tsadihv “tla gilo yigvyvhi galitsode gehe,” tsada ‘doyu yidotiluga gehv
segments.translation: That old lady, your sister, when we found each other, she come home with me. “Whose dog is it?” she said. “It’s mine,” I told her. “If you talk to him real good, he’ll be your best friend,” I told her. When we left and lived by Gentry, I would leave about 4:30 to go to work all day. “Do you know that when you go to work, that dog lays down by the front door?” she said. “Nobody can get in the house,” she said. It sure would get after you.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I guess that old lady taught him, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎥᎥ Ꮎ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᏍᏗ ᏧᎬᏩᎵᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎯᎠ ᏱᎦᏔ ᏱᎬᏅᎯᏓ ᎢᏯᏖᎾ *pork chop* ᏕᎦᎵᏗ ᏦᎢ ᎠᏕᎳ ᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ

segments.translation: Uh huh. The food, it was cheap back then. This big pork chop used to be just three dollars back then.

segments.text: “ᎨᎢ ‘Ꮲ ᏗᏟ ᏞᎦᏭ ᏱᏍᏓᏁᎳᏗ,” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ Wilmet Ꮎ *safari* ᎤᏬᏢ “ᎠᏎᏭ ᏱᎩ,” ᎤᏛᏅ Ꮎ ... “ᏱᏣᏝᏅᏓᏕ *pick up dead chickens*,” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ *I might pay you a little—little money,” Ꮎ ᏌᏊ ᏒᎯᏰ ᎨᎲ ᎠᎩᎷᏣ ᏗᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᏙᎸ ᏓᏭᏖᏐᏅ ᏥᏔᎦ Ꭰ’ᏗᏢ ᎤᎲ *barrel* ᎥᎾ ᏓᎩᎸᏅ ‘ᎡᎢ ᏓᏳᎦᏌᏔᏅ ᎯᎢ ᏱᎩᏓ *German Shepherd* “ᎩᎳᏴᏛ ᏙᏓᎬᏅᎵᏙᎵ Jim,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ Wali “ᏛᏰᏥᎸᏂᎵᏅᎮ ᎠᎭᏂ,” “ᏗᎠᎮ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᎦᏳᎳ ᎠᎩᏃᏎᎸ ᎠᎩᎵᏏ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ ᎪᎯᏛ ᏓᏳᎦᏌᏔᎾ ᎠᏭ ᎤᏬᏢ Ꮎ ᎩᏟ ᎠᏥᎪᎥ ᏙᎯ ᎥᎾ ᏗᏢ ᏭᎶᏒ ᏞᎦᏭᏛ *sniff around* ᏚᎾᏓᏛᏁᎴ ᏚᏓᎦᏘᎸᏒ Ꮎ German Shepherd ‘Ꮲ ᏓᏂᏙᎪ ᎾᎾᎵᏍᏗᎰ ᎪᎯᏴᏛ ᎤᏝᏅᏓᏕ Ꮎ ᎣᎩᎾᏤᎵ ᎩᏟ ᏍᏓᏱ ᏚᏂᏴᎲ Ꮎ German Shepherd ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᏭ ᏓᏥᎸᏛᏂᏍᏛᏂᏙᎸ
segments.transliteration: “gei ‘tlv ditli tlegawu yisdaneladi,” awohelv Wilmet na *safari* uwotlv “asewu yigi,” udvnv na ... “yitsatlanvdade *pick up dead chickens*,” awohelv *I might pay you a little—little money,” na saquu svhiye gehv agilutsa digilvwisdanedolv dawutesonv tsitaga a’ditlv uhv *barrel* vna dagilvnv ‘ei dayugasatanv hii yigida *German Shepherd* “gilayvdv dodagvnvlidoli Jim,” tsiyohelv Wali “dvyetsilvnilinvhe ahani,” “diahe” tsiyohelv “gayula aginoselv agilisi,” tsiyohehv gohidv dayugasatana awu uwotlv na gitli atsigov dohi vna ditlv wulosv tlegawudv *sniff around* dunadadvnele dudagatilvsv na German Shepherd ‘tlv danidogo nanalisdiho gohiyvdv utlanvdade na oginatseli gitli sdayi duniyvhv na German Shepherd nigalisdiwu datsilvdvnisdvnidolv
segments.translation: “If you all move over there,” said Wilmet—he owned the safari—“you all would live there for free.” “When you have time, pick up the dead chickens. I might pay you a little money,” he said. One evening when I came home from work, I started picking the chickens up. He had a barrel, and I put the chickens in there. There was a big German Shepherd that showed up. “I guess Jim will be fighting him pretty soon,” I told Wali. “He probably will get beat up right here,” she said. “I don’t think so,” I said. “My grandma already told me,” I said. After a while, the other dog was coming, and my dog was sitting there and he saw him. He got up real slow and walked toward it. It didn’t take long. He started sniffing it. The German Shepherd attacked, they were just standing up fighting. After a while, our dog had a chance, and he grabbed the German Shepherd hard and was just slinging it around.

segments.text: ᎠᏎᏅ ᎢᏓᏛᏁᎵᏍᎩᏭ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᎾᏛ.ᏐᏅ ‘Ꮲ ᎠᏂᏅ’Ꮲ ᎠᏬᏢ--ᏯᏬᏢ ᎠᏩᏛ.ᏓᏍᏗᏭ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᏂᏃᎮᏍᎬ...”ᏍᎩᏛ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏅᏬᏘ,” ᏍᎩᎾ ᏚᎾᏓᏙᎮᎸᏃ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎠᏩᏛᏓᏍᏗᏭ ᎨᎲ ᎥᎾ ᎠᏭᏖᏏᏙᎸ ᏥᎦᏔᎭ ᏅᏬᏘ

segments.translation: But when we were playing around, when I sat by the old men, I would listen to what they were talking about. When they’d say, “That medicine is a good medicine,” that’s when I really listened. What I know is just what I picked up here and there.

segments.text: Yeah. ᎾᏃᎲ uh...Ꮿ.ᏓᎲ ᏣᎪᎥ ᎤᏓᏁᏟᏴᏒ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏙᎲ ᎦᏙᎯ?

segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮿ.ᏓᎭ ᎡᏆ ᎤᏓᏁᏟᏴᏒ ᎠᎭᏂ ᎯᎦᏖᏃᎵᏙᎲ ᎦᏙᎯ? ᏏᎾ ᏥᏣᏛ.ᏏᏗᏒ? ᎤᎪᏗᏃ ᎤᏓᏁᏟᏴᏛ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: ya.daha equa udanetliyvsv ahani higatenolidohv gadohi? sina tsitsadv.sidisv? ugodino udanetliyvdv dohv?
segments.translation: Has this land changed a lot since you grew up? It has changed a lot, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Uh huh. Since my grandma died it just turned into woods.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It changed, mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Back then it was a big field.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I guess it was your grandma that did all the work. Ain’t it?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᏍᏓᏲᏏ ᏧᏂᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᎨᎲ ᏣᎾᏔ ᎨᎢ ᎠᏂ-Scott ᏣᏁᎮ?
segments.transliteration: sdayosi tsunilvwi,sdanehv gehv tsanata gei ani-Scott tsanehe?
segments.translation: They did work really hard. Did you know those Scotts that lived over there?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Uh huh.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᏥᏚᏂᎶᎨᏒ “ᎦᎷᏱᏍᏗᏭ ᏙᎩᎶᎨᏛ,” ᏣᏓ “ᏳᎯᏅ ᏗᎩᏛ *cross cu--cross cut* ᎣᏨᏛ ᏙᏣᎭᎴᏴᏍᎬ,” ᏣᏓ
segments.transliteration: tsidunilogesv “galuyisdiwu dogilogedv,” tsada “yuhinv digidv *cross cu--cross cut* otsvdv dotsahaleyvsgv,” tsada
segments.translation: They plowed a field. “We used axes,” she said. “We were using cross cut, cutting trees down,” she said.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ?Well, I’ll be... .... ᏂᎯᏍᎪᎲ... ᎤᎪᏓ Ꮵ.ᏕᎶ,ᏆᎡᎸ
segments.transliteration: na agayvlige?Well, I’ll be... .... nihisgohv... ugoda tsi.delo,quaelv
segments.translation: That old lady? Well, I’ll be... What you learned from the old lady...

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎤᎪᏓ Ꮵ.ᏕᎶ,ᏆᎡᎸ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏏᎨ. ᎬᏩ,ᏍᏗᏭ ᎲᏗᏍᎪ? Uh...ᎯᏕᎶ,ᏆᎡᎸ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: ugoda tsi.delo,quaelv agayvlige sige. gvwa,sdiwu hvdisgo? Uh...hidelo,quaelv agayvlige tsigehv
segments.translation: What you learned from the old lady, do you still use it?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: What is it?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎯᏕᎶ,ᏆᎡᎴᏛ ᎤᎪᏓ ᎲᏗᏍᎪᎨ ᏂᎯ ᏳᏓᎭ?
segments.transliteration: na agayvlige tsigehv hidelo,quaeledv ugoda hvdisgoge nihi yudaha?
segments.translation: The old lady, you learned a lot from her. Do you still use it?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᎯᏛ ᏥᏂᎬᏪᏍᎪ ᎠᎩᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏲᎩᎾᎵᎪ “ᎫᏍᏗ ᏱᏣᎴᏅ ᎭᏛᏁᎲ ᎮᏍᏗ ᏫᎵᏍᏛ. ᎫᏍᏗ ᏱᏭᎵ,ᏍᏆᏛ ᎩᎳ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎨᎮᏍᏗ,” ᎠᏗᎰ ᎦᏁᎵᏗᎰ ᎥᏍᎩ ᎾᏩᏛᏁ,Ꮧ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏱᎦᏛᏁᎭ
segments.transliteration: vv hidv tsinigvwesgo agilisi tsigehv yoginaligo “gusdi yitsalenv hadvnehv hesdi wilisdv. gusdi yiwuli,squadv gila nahiyu gehesdi,” adiho ganelidiho vsgi nawadvne,di gusdi yigadvneha
segments.translation: Yeah. My grandma used to say, “When you start doing something, don’t do it halfway. Always finish it.” I try to do that when I do something.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛᎲ ᏣᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᏛᎲ ᎠᏍᏓᏩᏗᏙᎯ ᎨᎲ ᏙᎲ? Ꮭ ᎠᏑᎵᎪᎩ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎬᏂ ᎩᎳ ᏭᎵ,ᏍᏆᏛ ᏍᎩᎾᎲ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏣᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: sgidvhv tsalisi tsigehv sgidvhv asdawadidohi gehv dohv? tla asuligogi yigehe gvni gila wuli,squadv sginahv nusdv tsalisi tsigehv
segments.translation: Your grandma, that’s what she followed, ain’t it? She did not quit until it was done. I guess that’s how she was when she did something.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Uh huh.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎩ,Ꮧ ᎨᎮ ᏙᎲ? ‘ᏴᏃ ᏧᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁ ᎨᎮ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: usquanigi,di gehe dohv? ‘yvno tsulvwisdane gehe agayvlige dohv?
segments.translation: That was very interesting. The old lady was really a hard worker, wasn’t she?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ ᏱᎦᏓᏅᏖᏍᎪ ... ᎣᎩᏁᎳᏛ ᎮᎾ ᏲᎦᏛᏁ,Ꮧ ᎤᏁᎳᏅᎯ ᏗᏢ ᎨᎵᎰ “’Ꮲ ᏱᏥᎨ.ᏲᎰ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏓᏅᎥᏍᎦ ᎯᏅᎰᏢ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎰ
segments.transliteration: sgina yigadanvtesgo ... ogineladv hena yogadvne,di unelanvhi ditlv geliho “’tlv yitsige.yoho nigalisdanvvsga hinvhotlv,” tsiyoheho
segments.translation: That’s what I think about. It was given to us to do in God’s way. I just pray, “Come and get me whenever You want.”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏳ,’Ꭱ ᏧᏓᏃᏣᏝ ᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏥᎨᎲ ... Ꮎ Ꮫ.ᎵᏏᎢ ᏗᎦᎴᏔᏅ ᎪᏪᎵ ᏣᏥᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ *newspaper*Ꭲ ... Yeah, ᏙᏳ’ᎡᎾ...ᏙᏳ ᎮᎾ ᎡᎳᏗ ᏗᏛᏂᎩᏍᎬ ᏧᏂᎳᏫ,ᏍᏗ ᎠᎪᏩ,Ꮫ.Ꮧ ᏥᎨᎰ ᎠᏭ, ᏧᏩᎦᏐᏒ ᏣᎢᏒ ᏧᎿᎷᏏᏗᏒ ... Ꮩ.Ꭿ ᏥᏓᏯᎢᏒ
segments.transliteration: doyu,’e tsudanotsatla gehv na agayvlige tsigehv ... na dv.lisii digaletanv goweli tsatsinohesgv saquu yuwaga,da sgina agayvlige *newspaper*i ... Yeah, doyu’ena...doyu hena eladi didvnigisgv tsunilawi,sdi agowa,dv.di tsigeho awu, tsuwagasosv tsaisv tsuhnalusidisv ... do.hi tsidayaisv
segments.translation: The old lady was really well known. One time, she was talked about in the Tulsa newspaper. Yeah, you could see her walking to church. She would be down and up the hills. You could see her coming up the hill real slow.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: [laughter]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh man.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᏧᏝᏂᎩᏓᏛ ᎠᏎ ᎨᎲ ᏧᏬᏰᏂ ᎯᏴᎮᏃ ᏥᎾᏕᏆ
segments.transliteration: tsutlanigidadv ase gehv tsuwoyeni hiyvheno tsinadequa
segments.translation: I guess her hands were real strong because they were this big.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Gah lee. Man. ... ᎯᎳᎩᏴ ᎤᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᎤᏍᏆᏛ ᏂᎯ ᏣᎾᏔ ᎨᎲ?
segments.transliteration: Gah lee. Man. ... hilagiyv udetiyvda gehv na usquadv nihi tsanata gehv?
segments.translation: Gah lee. Man. How old was she when she passed? As far as you know?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎯᎳᎩ ᎤᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏂᎯ ᏣᎾᏔ ᎨᎲ?
segments.transliteration: hilagi udetiyvda gehv sgina agayvlige nihi tsanata gehv?
segments.translation: As far as you know, how old was she?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏭᏛ ᏂᎦᎥ ᎠᏂᏃᎮᏍᎨ ᏍᎪᎯᏥ,--ᏍᎪᎯᏥ,Ꮚ ᏂᎦᏚ ᏣᏂᏗᎲ ᏍᎩᏭ ᎠᏩᎾᏙ. ᎠᏎᏃ Ꮎ ᏥᎬᏃᏎᎲ ᏗᎧᏃᎩᏍᏗ ᏍᎪᎯᏥᏊ ᏦᏍᎪᎯ ᏣᏗᎲ
segments.transliteration: sgiwudv nigav aninohesge sgohitsi,--sgohitsi,quu nigadu tsanidihv sgiwu awanado. aseno na tsigvnosehv dikanogisdi sgohitsiquu tsosgohi tsadihv
segments.translation: All I know is when they talk about her they say she was 114 years old. I was telling you about the musician he was saying that she was 130 years old.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: [whistles] I guess that’s when she was born, cause she walked the Trail.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Uh huh.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Old Cherokee [Referring to North Carolina] --

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎡᎵᏭ ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ ᏳᏛᏁ,Ꮧ ᏱᎩ ᎨᎵᎰ ᎠᏯ ᎨᎲ ᏯᏩᏓᏅᏖᏢ Ꮎ ᎤᏙ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏤᎩ ᎤᏛ.ᏐᏅ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: eliwu sgi hena yudvne,di yigi geliho aya gehv yawadanvtetlv na udo tsigehv tsegi udv.sonv tsigehv
segments.translation: I think she is about that old, when I think about it. Her brother, Tseg, he was really old.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Ain’t it?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎠᏥᏍᎦᏯᎬᎦ ᏍᏊ ... ᏍᎩᎾ ᏤᎩ ᏜᏱᎪ ᏗᏢ ᏥᎾᏛᏂᏗᎲ “ᎠᎹ Ꮭ ᎣᏍᏗ ᏱᎦᏛ.ᏗᏔᏍᏗ ᎥᎾᎾ ᎯᏫᎷᎦ,” ᎠᎪᎮᎴ ᎠᏭ Ꭸ.ᏓᎵ ᎤᏁᎩᏍᏗ ᎨᎮ ᎠᎹ ᎤᏗᏔᏍᏗ “ᏃᏊᎴ ᎨᏍᏗ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏱᏣᎵᎦᎳᏅ ᎠᏭ Ꮵ.ᏁᎸ,” ᎠᎪᎮᎸ
segments.transliteration: atsisgayagvga squu ... sgina tsegi dlayigo ditlv tsinadvnidihv “ama tla osdi yigadv.ditasdi vnana hiwiluga,” agohele awu ge.dali unegisdi gehe ama uditasdi “noquule gesdi gusdi yitsaligalanv awu tsi.nelv,” agohelv
segments.translation: She was still getting onto him, Tseg. He would go toward Jay. “The water is not good to drink,” she would tell him. He used to get it, water to drink, from down the hill. “And you’re not paying rent living there,” she told him.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Man.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎤᏘᎾᏫᏛᎮ ᎤᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏕᏂᎵ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᎢᎪᎯᏓ ᏱᏚᏪᏘᏅ ᏥᏭᎵᏬᏨ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ ᏣᎵ ᏣᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎯᏲᎵᎦ ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: utinawidvhe usdayvhvsgi noquule denili tsigehv tla sgi igohida yiduwetinv tsiwuliwotsv tsuyohusv tsali tsadv tsigehv hiyoliga gehv
segments.translation: He took his wife and also Daniel. He didn’t last long, he died, he passed away. Did you know George?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, I saw him.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᏝᏍᏊ ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎩ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎯᎢ ᏥᏂᎦᏔ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎥᏥᏅᏮᏅ ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎩ ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᏣᏓ ᏍᎩ ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎩ,Ꮣ
segments.transliteration: tlasquu gawonisgi yigehe tsadihv hii tsinigata tsadihv vtsinvwvnv gawonisgi nuli,stanv tsada sgi usquanigi,da
segments.translation: He wasn’t talking when he was about this tall [indicates]. I healed him and he started talking. That is interesting..

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: He knew.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: ...What he knows.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: I guess because he was asking, he got help.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏓᏙᎵᏍᏗᎲ ... ᏙᎲ ᎤᏝᏂᎩᏓ ᎨᎲ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏙᎲ? Man... ᎿᏃᎲ uh...ᏳᏓᏍᏓᏴᏅ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏥᎨᎲ ‘ᏙᎲ ᎤᏍᏗ uh...ᏂᎯ ᏣᎾᏔ ᎨᎲ ‘ᏙᎲ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎪᏢᏍᎨ ᎠᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ? ᏧᏓᎴᏅᏓᎨ. Ꭼ--?
segments.transliteration: adadolisdihv ... dohv utlanigida gehv agayvlige dohv? Man... hnanohv uh...yudasdayvnv agayvlige tsigehv ‘dohv usdi uh...nihi tsanata gehv ‘dohv usdi osda gotlvsge ali,sdayv,di? tsudalenvdage. gv--?
segments.translation: Yeah, he was praying. The old lady was a strong woman, wasn’t she? When the old lady cooked, what do you know that she cooked really well? Or was it just all kinds of things?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎠᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴ,ᏗᎩ? ... ᏧᏓᎴᏅᏓ ᎠᎦᏔᎲ hom—hominy ᏱᎩ ᎤᏩᏌ ᎪᏢᏍᎬ ᏃᏊᎴᏅ ᏗᏤᎢ ᏎᎷ ᏥᏓ--ᏥᏓᏛ.ᏍᎪ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ Ꮩ--ᏫᏙᎦᎵᎰ ᏓᎦ,ᏠᏗᎰ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏎᎷ ᏧᏬᎭᏄᎶᏔᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏗᎦᎪᏇᏅᏍᎪ *pan* ᏱᎩ.Ꮣ ᎠᎭᏂ ᎠᎹ ᎠᏟᏍᏓ ᎠᎹ ᏙᎦᏢᏍᎪ ᏙᎬᏂᏍᏗᎲ ᎤᏂᏖᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏗᎩᏍᏗ.
segments.transliteration: ali,sdayv,digi? ... tsudalenvda agatahv hom—hominy yigi uwasa gotlvsgv noquulenv ditsei selu tsida--tsidadv.sgo sgiyusdi do--widogaliho daga,tlodiho sgina selu tsuwohanulotanv sgina digagoquenvsgo *pan* yigi.da ahani ama atlisda ama dogatlvsgo dogvnisdihv unitedi gehv nowu sgina digisdi.
segments.translation: Food? It was all different things. Black hominy—she made it herself. There was new corn ready to pick and she would get those and shuck them. And she would wrap corn in the shucks and cook them. She had a big pan with water and she put salt in it and then the corn and they were really good to eat.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: [ᎤᏰᏥᏍᎦ] ᏍᎩᎨ. ᏭᎪᏛ ᏣᎸᏉ,Ꮧ ᎨᏎ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᏣᎩᏍᏗ?
segments.transliteration: [uyetsisga] sgige. wugodv tsalvquo,di gese sgiyusdi tsagisdi?
segments.translation: [laughs] Is that what you liked the best to eat?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Uh huh.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏍᎪ? Well, I’ll be... Yeah, mhm... ᏝᎲ Ꭹ.Ꮆ ᏱᎬᎪᏢᎾ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᏃᏭ ᏙᎲ? Ꮭ
segments.transliteration: dosgo? Well, I’ll be... Yeah, mhm... tlahv gi.lo yigvgotlvna sgiyusdi nowu dohv? tla
segments.translation: Well, I’ll be... I guess nobody makes this stuff anymore.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Nobody knows how.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎯᏯᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪᏍ ᎡᏘᏴ ᏜᏱᎪ ᏤᎮ uh...’Ꮩ ᏥᏚᏙᎥ? Uh...ᎦᏚ ᏥᏕᎪᏢᏍᎬ ᏃᏊᎴ
segments.transliteration: hiyanvdadisgos etiyv dlayigo tsehe uh...’do tsidudov? Uh...gadu tsidegotlvsgv noquule
segments.translation: Did you know he lived in Jay? What was his name...? He used to make bread?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: What is it?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꭱ ᎡᏘᏴ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏤᎲ ᏜᏱᎪ McClemore ᏧᏙᎢᏓ Yeah. ᏥᏕᎪᏢᏍᎬ Ꮎ ᏥᏕᎦᏇᎾᏗᎰᎢᏅ Ꮎ ᎤᏖᏗ ᏗᎩᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.transliteration: na’e etiyv tsigehv tsehv dlayigo McClemore tsudoida Yeah. tsidegotlvsgv na tsidegaquenadihoinv na utedi digisdi sgina
segments.translation: He lived in Jay a long time ago. His name is McClemore. He used to make bread, he used to wrap them up. And they were good to eat.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Uh huh.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: How about your grandma? Did she make anything like that?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: She was making them.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᎢᏳᏍᏗᏭ ᏥᎩ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏴᎪᏢᎾ ᎠᎦ,ᏔᎭ ᎠᎩᎵᏏ
segments.transliteration: iyusdiwu tsigi gusdi yvgotlvna aga,taha agilisi
segments.translation: She knew how to make all kinds of things.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, man. Boy, ᏙᏳ,ᏛᎲ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎠᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ ᎨᎮ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: Yeah, man. Boy, doyu,dvhv osda ali,sdayv,di gehe nahiyu dohv?
segments.translation: It was good food to eat back then, wasn’t it?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.text: ᏳᎪᏛᎮ ᏗᎦᏝᏂᎬᎮ ᏍᎩ ᎢᎦ ᎡᎵ ᏱᏓᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎦ
segments.transliteration: yugodvhe digatlanigvhe sgi iga eli yidali,sdayvhvsga
segments.translation: We would have probably been stronger if we were eating like that today.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Gah lee. Yeah, yeah. ᏝᏃ ᏍᎩ ᎢᎦ ᎤᏢᎩ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏍᏊ ᏣᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ?
segments.transliteration: Gah lee. Yeah, yeah. tlano sgi iga utlvgi yigehe squu tsalisi tsigehv?
segments.translation: And your grandma, she hardly ever got sick, didn’t she?

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Huh uh.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮩ.Ꭿ ᎡᎮ ᎨᎮ ᏙᎲ? Yeah...ᎾᏛᎲ ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎬ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎬᏂᏍᏗᏍᎨ ᎡᏍᎦ ᎾᏓᏛᏁ ᏂᎨᏒᎾ ᎣᏰᎸ
segments.transliteration: do.hi ehe gehe dohv? Yeah...nadvhv adasdayvhvsgv osda gvnisdisge esga nadadvne nigesvna oyelv
segments.translation: She was really well all the time. I guess the things she was cooking was good for your body.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Interesting. Well... I appreciate it. I appreciate it.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Me too. I appreciate us talking.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᎠᏯᏛᏍᏊ ᏙᏳ ᎮᎾ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎢᎾᏝᏃᎲᎳ ᎪᎯᎨ ᎬᎦᏝᏃᎮᏢ ᎨᎮ
segments.transliteration: Yeah, ayadvsquu doyu hena osda inatlanohvla gohige gvgatlanohetlv gehe
segments.translation: Me too. We really had a good talk. We haven’t talked in a long time.

segments.speaker: toney-cornshucker
segments.translation: Uh huh.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Well, I appreciate it.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: I appreciate it.
